messages:
liam: seeing an odd pattern in ap-southeast1 around 06:10 UTC — lots of tiny pods (gpu-tiny) evicted during autoscaler scale-down. anyone else? :thinking:
anika: yup i clipped the scheduler logs — looks like nodes with the `gpu-anchored=true` annotation were still considered deletable by asg-scale-down
kai: that annotation is supposed to make nodes sticky for long-running tiny-gang jobs. did we change anything in the scale-down predicate?
ops-bot: alert: cluster-autoscaler: scaleDown candidates 12 -> 3 in ap-southeast1 at 06:08 UTC (policy: aggressive-scale-test).
liam: pasted a quick snippet i pulled from scheduler:```
E0305 06:09:12 scheduler_predicate.go:423] Node gpu-node-apse1-42 considered for scale-down: occupied by 2 pods (both annotated gpu-anchored=true) but RemovePodsViolatesInterPodAffinity=false -> marked deletable
```
sarah: that RemovePodsViolatesInterPodAffinity check shouldn't be bypassable. who pushed the aggressive-scale-test policy?
infra-bot: policy-push: aggressive-scale-test by chris@infra (change-id: pol-2026-03-05-99). Modified `scaleDownUtilizationThreshold` from 0.5 -> 0.2 and `unneededTime` 10m -> 2m.
chris: i rolled that policy for a cost experiment to see warm-pool delta. wasn't expecting it to pick nodes with gpu-anchored jobs. my bad, rolling back now.
anika: rollback please. tight window - these tiny jobs checkpoint poorly and we lose progress on preempt.
kai: mitigation: i can temporarily annotate those tiny-gang podsets with `prevent-scale-down=true` and taint the nodes `no-scale-down=true:NoSchedule` then remove after 1h. cheap and quick
liam: quick kubectl paste of affected pods:```
$ kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | grep gpu-tiny
gpu-train-4  0/1 Evicted  1   7m gpu-node-apse1-42
gpu-train-5  0/1 Evicted  1   7m gpu-node-apse1-42
```
sarah: cost note: if we hold nodes to avoid evictions it'll add ~6-8 hours of billed time for those nodes (~$420/node). small experiment but flag for finance
ops-bot: action created: AUTOSCALE-221 investigate policy push + rollback (assigned to chris).
chris: rollback applied. reverting `unneededTime` -> 10m and `scaleDownUtilizationThreshold` -> 0.5. monitoring now.
anika: ack. also proposing a longer-term fix: cluster-autoscaler should respect `gpu-anchored` annotation (existing, but looks like our predicate patch lost it). open to a PR to reintroduce explicit check
kai: on that PR, also add integration test with warmpool + tiny-gang mix. we missed that in canary
liam: metrics: pod_evictions spiked 180 -> 12 in 5m after policy apply. after rollback it's back to 8 -> trending down. good sign
sarah: please run a quick replay on the scheduler logs for consistency and collect `kubelet` events for the evicted pods. we'll need timestamps for the postmortem
chris: creating a follow-up: AUTOSCALE-222 add explicit `gpu-anchored` predicate + integration test. assigning to kai
anika: also a short-term automation: when `unneededTime` < 5m we automatically set a cluster-level override to ignore `gpu-anchored=false` nodes or pause aggressive policies. less friction for cost experiments
kai: i like that. we can gate it behind a feature-flag so ops can run experiments safely
liam: recap: cause = experiment policy with too-low unneededTime + lowered threshold -> autoscaler removed nodes holding gpu-anchored pods -> evictions; mitigation = rollback policy + temporary taint/annotation and abort scale-down; next = PR for predicate + integration tests + feature-flag guard
sarah: i'll draft a short incident blurb for #all-hands with cost impact and jobs affected. please add the job ids for checkpoint restores (we lost 3 long runs)
anika: job ids: 4521, 4522, 4523. recommend restart with latest checkpoints once nodes stable
chris: admitting the rollout without a canary was a mistake. will follow up on rollout checklist updates
liam: thanks all. i'll watch for residual preempts and close AUTOSCALE-221 after logs and kubelet events are uploaded
ops-bot: AUTOSCALE-221 status: in progress -> monitoring
anika: one more note: consider adding scheduler metric alert for "scale-down evictions/sec > X" so we catch this earlier
kai: filed a small ticket: MON-998 add evictions/sec alert for GPU pools. tagging oncall.
liam: end state: nodes stable, eviction rate returning to baseline, policy rollback in place.
